title: Simple user management: This module lets non-administrators approve, deactivate and delete users, limited by the roles they can delegate through Role Delegation. (CVE-2026-114543)
description: The Simple User Management module for Drupal allows non-administrators to approve, deactivate, and delete users based on delegated roles. However, it insufficiently verifies role delegation when approving users and provides an Activate link for blocked administrators. Additionally, it does not protect the primary user (user 1) from deactivation or deletion. Exploitation requires the attacker to have a role with specific module action permissions.
aiSummary: The vulnerability in the Drupal Simple User Management module (CVE-2026-114543) arises from inadequate checks on role delegation during user approval processes. This flaw allows non-administrators with delegated permissions to approve users without sufficient validation, potentially activating blocked administrators. Furthermore, the module lacks safeguards to prevent deactivation or deletion of the primary user account (user 1). The risk is mitigated by the prerequisite that an attacker must already possess a role with the module's additional action permissions.
aiImpact: An attacker with a role that includes the module's additional action permissions could approve users improperly, activate blocked administrators, or deactivate/delete critical user accounts including user 1. This could lead to unauthorized account management actions within the Drupal environment, potentially compromising administrative control.
